title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being adopted for NetOps tasks: intent translation, configuration synthesis, change planning, and limited automated repair. Operational safety for applied NetOps systems depends as much on surrounding engineering (deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, rollback) as on the model’s raw proposal quality. A standard operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and repairs or human interventions remediate violations. Despite broad consensus that guardrails are necessary, practitioners lack controlled measurements that isolate the verifier’s marginal contribution while holding the model output fixed. This gap makes it difficult to budget verification/repair costs versus generation alternatives (e.g., regeneration under verifier guidance).

We answer a narrowly scoped, operational question under tightly controlled semantics: given identical initial LLM proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected high/medium-severity violations compared to the same LLM alone? We preregistered the design, executed the run, and archived all artifacts. The experiment purposefully constrains model, verifier coverage, and repair budget to isolate the verifier’s marginal effect under plausible deployment semantics where preserving the original proposal is required or where regeneration is expensive.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-configuration verifiers have a long history in the systems and formal-methods communities: header-space analyses and Batfish-style tools can statically check reachability, isolation, and update-safety properties and have been shown to detect subtle misconfigurations pre-deployment. Concurrently, recent NetOps and AIOps work demonstrates LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while emphasizing guardrails and mixed human–AI workflows. Generate–verify–repair (or generate–critic) patterns appear across structured-generation domains and have been proposed to reduce unsafe outputs. Separate literature catalogs LLM failure modes in system contexts (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends deterministic verification and human oversight as mitigations. What is less represented are preregistered, paired ablations that quantify the verifier’s marginal effect under matched initial proposals; our experiment fills that specific measurement gap and situates findings relative to both classical verification tools and recent LLM–NetOps system reports.
sections.methodology:
Design overview and preregistration. We preregistered the study (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026) and locked seeds, inclusion rules, estimands, analysis procedures, and stopping criteria before data collection. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success = verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The confirmatory inferential test was a preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs; complementary uncertainty was quantified via paired-bootstrap percentile CIs (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) preserving pairing.

Task corpus and stratification. We used a deterministic synthetic generator to produce 500 intent→configuration tasks deterministically stratified into three clusters: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166). Generator constraints limited task payloads to verifier-modeled features allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}, ensuring construct validity with respect to what the verifier could check. No preregistered confirmatory exclusions occurred; all 500 preregistered pairs completed.

Generation semantics and controls. To isolate verifier marginal effect we adopted shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single LLM proposal per task (the shared initial generation) served as both the baseline output and the guarded arm’s input. The guarded arm invoked at most one automated repair iteration only when the deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged a preregistered high/ or medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. This prevents conflating verifier impact with verifier-guided regeneration or multi-iteration repair policies and aligns with deployment scenarios that preserve the original candidate for human review while applying minimal automated fixes.

Modeling, verifier, and operational constraints. The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini (hosted adapter); single-attempt generation and a 2000-token output limit were enforced. The deterministic verifier maps concrete violation codes to severities and evaluates a predefined property set; success is defined relative to that modeled coverage. The repair policy permitted at most one automated repair iteration per flagged candidate. The preregistered retry and missingness policies governed transient provider failures and were followed exactly during execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run processed the 500 complete preregistered pairs under the shared_initial_candidate design. Execution manifest recorded model_calls_used = 501 (500 shared-initial generations + 1 repair-stage call) with zero failed hosted model calls. Aggregated condition summaries: baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline success rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 499 (both pass), n10 = 1 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), n00 = 0 (both fail). Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Inferential and resampling results. Under the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention the two-sided McNemar p-value for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1) is p = 1.00. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). These analyses follow the preregistered estimand and implementation rules archived with the run.

Repair activity and corrected episode provenance. The guarded arm invoked a single repair-stage call; that repair produced the sole discordant outcome (the single task where the baseline failed and the guarded arm passed). Per-task validator traces and the execution manifest confirm exactly one corrected episode in the confirmatory set. Representative per-task artifacts in the evidence bundle include the validator violation codes and the repair prompt/response for that episode.

Power and sensitivity. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure prevalence ≈ 30% to detect a 10-percentage-point absolute reduction with 80% power (N ≈ 384). Observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower, producing a ceiling effect that substantially reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. As a result secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts and are reported as empty in the preregistered analysis outputs.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation and operational meaning. Under the constrained experimental regime—single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, verifier coverage limited to {admin, mtu, vlan}, and at most one automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling verified proposals and the marginal pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier+single-repair budget was small (point estimate 0.002). This is not a general claim about all model–verifier pairings or unconstrained production workloads; it is a conditional measurement that informs operational trade-offs when baseline proposal quality for verifier-scoped properties is already high.

What the result implies for deployment decisions. First, when baseline verifier-scoped error prevalence is extremely low, modest investments in automated repair (single iteration) yield limited marginal pass-rate gains; resources may be better allocated to expanding verifier coverage, increasing repair budget, or enabling verifier-guided regeneration. Second, preserving shared_initial_candidate semantics is appropriate where preserving the original proposal for human review is required or when model-call costs are tightly constrained: it minimizes model-call overhead (observed model_calls_used = 501 for 500 pairs). Third, the verifier still provided operational value by correcting a concrete, rare baseline failure.

Limitations and threats to validity. Construct validity is bounded by the verifier’s modeled property set: success is defined with respect to the verifier’s coverage and severity mapping; properties outside that set (vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies, dynamic protocol state) are not measured here. External validity is limited by single-model testing (gpt-5-mini requested), a synthetic deterministic task corpus, and limited repair budget (max 1 iteration). The very low observed baseline failure rate caused a ceiling effect that reduces power to detect modest absolute improvements; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the preregistered exact-binomial convention in the small-discordant count regime. These limitations are described in the preregistration and evidence bundle, which also contains the full raw per-task diagnostics for re-inspection.

Recommendations for future measurement and practice. Measure baseline verifier-scoped error prevalence on representative operational data before selecting a repair budget: low prevalence constrains marginal return. If operators require broader safety guarantees, expand verifier-modeled properties and consider alternative semantics (verifier-guided regeneration or greater repair iteration budgets) and perform separate preregistered comparisons under those semantics. Finally, include cost accounting (model-call latency, repair latency) alongside pass/fail metrics when evaluating generation semantics in production decision-making.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.006] and an archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the preregistered exact-binomial convention. The measurement demonstrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is already very high for the verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is narrow, a modest verifier+repair budget yields limited measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric while still correcting rare concrete failures. Practitioners should first estimate baseline error prevalence for verifier-scoped properties, align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints, and select generation/repair semantics that reflect deployment cost and review requirements. The full preregistration, execution traces, per-task validator diagnostics, repair prompts/responses, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every factual claim above.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task corpus limited to the verifier-modeled features; task payloads were constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, wider cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or dynamic protocol states outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — we do not claim multi-model or cross-validator generality.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) induced a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in the study evidence bundle. The run-level manifest and per-task scoring traces confirm exactly one such corrected episode in the confirmatory set.
